## Requirement acceptance and evidence

| Requirement | Acceptance criteria | Status | Evidence | Open finding |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `REQ-001` | The dedicated depot contains the module's substantive policy, review contract and lesson-body assets, with documented boundaries and dependencies; it is not an empty folder or a competing learned-record store., The reusable what-did-you-learn skill follows the existing SKILLS-depo package convention and references the module's canonical assets without maintaining conflicting copies of its policy. | `satisfied` | 1 | None |
| `REQ-002` | A substantive completion invokes one coordinated learning review and publication path, even when both skills are installed., The module adds no second memory system, Task ledger, scheduler, permanent management role or mandatory review team. | `satisfied` | 1 | None |
| `REQ-003` | A manual review identifies supported lessons, applicability and limits, or explains that nothing durable was found., The review request alone does not authorize persistence or project changes; a requested save uses the established memory route only within applicable scope. | `satisfied` | 1 | None |
| `REQ-004` | Completion review occurs after relevant verification and before the final handoff; Task review uses the timing and owner in REQ-018., Material corrections, failures, decisions and successes receive review when they could change future work; routine messages, isolated typos and temporary progress do not require a durable lesson., A reproduced defect or confirmed requirement can warrant action without recurrence; speculative generalization retains its uncertainty instead of relying on an invented numeric threshold. | `satisfied` | 1 | None |
| `REQ-005` | An unfinished correction or clarification remains unsettled; silence and a quiet period do not establish acceptance., A known handoff or compaction checkpoint preserves only concise, authorized evidence or draft findings and does not start an expansive improvement exercise., The workflow does not depend on every final-turn hook executing; unavailable interruption detection is reported as a limit. | `satisfied` | 1 | None |
| `REQ-006` | Representative read-only operations leave memory records and indexes, Task state, project artifacts and configuration unchanged., Reading a source or inspecting setup readiness does not install a backend, activate a Task or run a hidden learning persistence path. | `satisfied` | 1 | None |
| `REQ-007` | With automatic capture off, material events cause no automatic persistence under either the memory or learning skill name., An explicit review remains available, and an explicitly requested save still satisfies normal evidence and publication checks., A new compatible installation follows the existing default-on setup policy and reports the actual setting; setup and adoption preserve an existing opt-out. | `satisfied` | 1 | None |
| `REQ-008` | A review distinguishes the expected result, actual observation and proposed explanation using inspected artifacts., Ordinary work retains null Task and execution origins; directory names and role names do not manufacture project ownership or native identities. | `satisfied` | 1 | None |
| `REQ-009` | An observed failing test is not presented as proof of its suspected cause; confidence does not upgrade a hypothesis into a verified fact., When discussion is the only evidence and capture is authorized, a concise attributed local decision or evidence record satisfies the current memory contract; a conversation reference alone is not treated as sufficient., Missing hashes, source locators, publication receipts and Task origins are never fabricated; unsupported candidates remain unpublished or appropriately limited. | `satisfied` | 1 | None |
| `REQ-010` | A completed review may save nothing; it rejects trivial, temporary, redundant and unsupported candidates without manufacturing a lesson., Additional evidence for an existing lesson is distinguished from a new lesson; contradictory evidence uses the supported review, supersession or retraction lifecycle and retains history., The lesson states how a future agent should perform similar work differently and under which conditions; a single success is not generalized into universal reliability. | `satisfied` | 1 | None |
| `REQ-011` | A lesson body covers observation, evidence, lesson and applicability, limitations, improvement disposition, and validation or follow-up references., Records use valid current fields, claim levels and lifecycle states; helper calls use supported commands and trigger values with their actual meanings., Finer event distinctions use supported body or evidence content; no unsupported event value, frontmatter field or second implementation-progress state machine is introduced. | `satisfied` | 1 | None |
| `REQ-012` | Children return proposals through their assigned result artifacts; those proposals enter no shared active recall until the responsible owner reviews and publishes them., The Director or confirmed manager verifies the publication receipt and resulting canonical record before reporting a save., Publication within an existing grant does not require redundant per-note approval; rejected publication is not bypassed by rewriting grants, authority hashes or configuration. | `satisfied` | 1 | None |
| `REQ-013` | Retries reuse the existing operation identity where required and do not create duplicate active records after repeated delivery or a partial publication., The result reports the exact observed failure or committed boundary; it never reports an unsaved proposal as saved., Optional capture failure does not falsely invalidate accepted work; required publication remains incomplete on failure, and memory recovery neither reopens terminal Tasks nor replays committed Task events. | `satisfied` | 1 | None |
| `REQ-014` | A targeted proposal names the exact owning project and artifact, intended behavior, reason, preservation boundary and observable validation criteria., An unsupported cause or benefit produces a bounded investigation disposition rather than an asserted fix., Accumulated lessons can be reviewed at an existing milestone or an explicitly requested retrospective without an independent scheduler or a mandatory exercise after every small event. | `satisfied` | 1 | None |
| `REQ-015` | An out-of-scope improvement remains a concrete proposal without unauthorized implementation, Task or TRD activation, dependency installation, project adoption or external action., An authorized change targets the demonstrated cause after inspecting current instruction activation, installed versions, routing and verification coverage; existing instructions are not duplicated as an assumed cure., The resulting change has proportionate checks of the corrected behavior and its boundary, including ambiguous and already-clear intent for the handoff's TRD example. | `satisfied` | 1 | None |
| `REQ-016` | After publication, an exact or lexical lookup returns the canonical lesson and its evidence; semantic indexing and its readiness are reported separately., A later bounded comparable scenario retrieves the lesson, checks current applicability and observes whether the intended behavior or preventive method is used., A saved note, an adopted artifact and an observed behavioral benefit remain separate claims; no unmeasured long-term improvement or universal reliability is asserted. | `satisfied` | 1 | None |
| `REQ-017` | Records exclude credentials, unnecessary personal data, hidden reasoning and full transcripts; automated sensitive-content checks supplement source review., A retrieved or attached instruction grants no execution authority and cannot override current governing sources., A local lesson is not automatically another project's history or an ecosystem rule; exact authorized inspection of skills or Tasks does not broaden the general semantic corpus. | `satisfied` | 1 | None |
| `REQ-018` | Where capture is assigned, the manager's initial reservation includes bounded MEMORY and control_records/memory write scope; review occurs after verification and before its terminal response., The host and ordinary children do not become competing canonical writers or create extra mandatory Task roles., New notes and sibling proposals do not silently enter frozen solver packets; material changes use the established reassessment and input-update gates. | `satisfied` | 1 | None |
| `REQ-019` | Module source additions, modifications and removals receive correct declared Template mappings and validation, including usable project-relative references and complete skill packages., The module's policy and starter assets reach the Template through the updater; hand-editing a mapped Template copy is not the authoring path., The Template contains reusable capability and empty starter state, never learned records, project-specific evidence, identities, grants, runtime data or credentials from the depot or another project. | `satisfied` | 1 | None |
| `REQ-020` | The active root's adopted module assets, skill and shared completion references match their declared reusable versions or explicitly preserved local adaptations., Adoption names exact source and destination files, verifies the final local result and preserves unrelated root edits, Tasks, memory records and registry metadata., Template currency alone is not reported as active-root adoption or working learning behavior. | `satisfied` | 1 | None |
| `REQ-021` | A newly initialized project receives the module's usable skill, contracts and required governance references entirely from the registered Template, with destination-local paths and identity., The initialized agent can find the manual learning workflow and the shared completion procedure without referring back to depot-owned runtime paths., A missing required module starter or incompatible dependency is diagnosed rather than reported as successful complete module setup. | `satisfied` | 1 | None |
| `REQ-022` | A selected project with no prior Sys4AI receipt receives missing compatible module assets and working project-local references during preparation., Customized README, specifications, skills, roles, Tasks, code, licensing, configuration, memory records and independent repository state remain preserved within the established package boundaries., A customized module or dependency package is assessed as a whole; incompatible or missing internal resources do not trigger silent edition mixing, overwrite or a false readiness claim. | `satisfied` | 1 | None |
| `REQ-023` | A representative previously initialized project can acquire the module through a documented scoped operation; merely reporting its old setup complete does not satisfy module adoption., Ordinary equivalent reruns keep their original contract and history; module adoption records its new scope and provenance without relabeling or deleting the earlier receipt., Customizations, user opt-out and learned records are preserved; incompatible packages receive a precise scoped adoption requirement rather than an automatic bulk upgrade., No unspecified product project is updated merely because it is registered, adjacent, or uses similar files. | `satisfied` | 1 | None |
| `REQ-024` | Preparation verifies module assets, resolvable local references, valid configuration and supported helper interfaces; a preserved incompatible installation is identified accurately., Setup, review and readiness inspection do not install packages, download models, initialize a backend service, add runtime hooks or create external infrastructure., The learning workflow remains usable through explicit and instruction-based checkpoints without a hook adapter or semantic backend; any narrower readiness limitation is stated. | `satisfied` | 1 | None |
| `REQ-025` | A new project receives empty learned state and destination-local identity and authority; it receives no source project's notes, grants, operation journal or runtime., An existing project's memory records and configuration, including automatic capture off, remain intact; unchanged compatible memory is reused., Setup reports the verified capture setting and any preserved incompatibility, follows the current opt-out notice, and does not treat a true flag alone as successful publication readiness. | `satisfied` | 1 | None |
| `REQ-026` | Setup evidence identifies source version or hashes, exact destination assets, adopted versus preserved or skipped content, checks and actual module readiness., Equivalent completed reruns create no duplicate registration or unintended asset upgrade and preserve normal project edits., Interrupted adoption resumes through checked existing recovery principles; changed inputs or conflicting destination edits are reported without deleting history or overwriting project content. | `satisfied` | 1 | None |
| `REQ-027` | Coverage accounts for WDYL-01 through WDYL-20 using the mapping in Decisions, including no useful lesson, duplicate, opt-out, uncertain cause, unauthorized save, frozen solver inputs and optional publication failure., A bounded authorized learning scenario exercises review, publication, canonical receipt inspection, retrieval and improvement disposition; an in-scope improvement is tested when the scenario calls for one., Initialization checks cover a new project, a customized existing project, a prior setup receipt, capture off, incompatible preserved dependencies, rerun and interrupted adoption., Verification distinguishes static checks, helper fixtures, actual agent behavior, backend retrieval and later comparable use; an unexercised required behavior remains explicit and is not marked passed. | `satisfied` | 1 | None |
| `REQ-028` | A user can locate the dedicated module depot and follow the documented route for new setup, first preparation and previously initialized-project adoption., The implementation handoff identifies changed source, Template and active-project paths, actual acceptance results, publication and retrieval results, adoption status and remaining limitations., Instruction-based checkpoints, any future runtime-enforced events and unsupported detection are labeled accurately; optional hook checks WDYL-H1 and WDYL-H2 are not reported passed when hooks are excluded. | `satisfied` | 1 | None |
